summary: Daud Ali is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the College of William & Mary and under Ronald Inden at the University of Chicago, later holding posts at SOAS (~1995–2009) and the University of Pennsylvania (2009).

Daud Rahbar was a religious studies scholar who studied at Government College University, Lahore, and Cambridge. He held posts at Punjab, Oriental College, McGill, Ankara, Wisconsin-Madison, and Boston University (~1968–1999).
David A. Dilworth is a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968).

David A. Hall works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shōshin Ichishima and earned a doctorate at UC Berkeley (1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).
David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He held posts at Rice University and Santa Clara University (attested 2008–2017).

David Brown was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Joseph Milner and at Magdalene College, Cambridge. He served as Provost of Fort William College (1800) and founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society.

David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Western Sydney University and served as Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000).

David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997) and became a Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

David Dean Shulman is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned degrees from Hebrew University of Jerusalem and SOAS/University of London under John Ralston Marr. He held positions at Hebrew University (1976; 1985–2017) and the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (1992–1998).

David Drewes is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Lawrence University, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia (PhD 2006 under Karen C. Lang). He taught at Virginia, Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2006), and the University of Manitoba (attested 2009–2010).

David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at UCLA. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and Hawaiʻi, and held research posts at Nichibunken (attested 2006) and Oberlin (attested 2010).

David Edward Cooper is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St Edmund Hall. He was a lecturer at Oxford (1967), Professor of Philosophy at Durham (1986–2008), and a visiting professor at Peking University (2022).

David Fiordalis specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Carleton College, Chicago, and Michigan (PhD under Luis O. Gómez). He is an associate professor and department chair at Linfield University (attested 2017).
David Forbes held faculty positions at Brooklyn College and affiliate faculty status at the Graduate Center, CUNY (both attested 2016).
David Friedman was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS (~1950–1970) and as Professor at the University of London (attested 1969).

David Gellner is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Oxford (attested 1988; Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology attested 2026) and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

David Germano is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1992) and has served on the faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 2000–2008 and 2026).
David Gonsalez is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Gen Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Wisconsin-Madison, Banaras Hindu, Sorbonne, and Chicago (PhD under Kali Charan Bahl). He held posts at Chicago, Virginia (1986, 1994–1996), and UC Santa Barbara (1996, 2000).
